verdicts.note: Repeated explicit pledges across statement, website and the Herald-Republic: no plea-downs for gang violence, every sentencing enhancement, full prosecution of repeat offenders, 'enforce the law firmly ... without apology' [S1][S2][S3]. -2 high holds.
First-time candidate whose legal career is shorter than his opponent's, though he cites nearly 19 years in the criminal-justice system and current prosecution work [S1][S2]. -1 medium holds.

'Public safety, accountability, and strong partnerships with law enforcement' and holding offenders accountable [S1][S2], set against her stated balanced view from defense and pro tem judge work [S1]. Enforcement-leaning but less specific than her opponent: -1 medium holds.

She has the longer legal record (practicing since 2008; county deputy prosecutor and unit supervisor 2008-2011; more than 65 trials; municipal prosecutor since 2022) [S1][S4], so she leans further toward proven record than her opponent. But she holds no elected office and has no enacted record, and her county prosecution service ended in 2011 [S4]; -2 is reserved for long tenure with an enacted record. -1 medium, with the relative difference carried by the dossiers.
